Utilizing an array of imaging methods, the center is able to rapidly identify potential crystallization hits, having already conducted over 25 million experiments on more than 17,000 samples. The Cryo-EM Center, on the other hand, is equipped with advanced technology such as the Glacios 200 kV microscope, Volta phase plate, and Falcon 4 and Ceta-D detectors to produce high-quality data. The independent, non-profit institute, founded in 1956, is made up of a dedicated team of researchers committed to improving health through structural biology research. It has a rich history of innovation and education and is a founding institute of the Buffalo Niagara Medical Campus.
